money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Lari (GEL). When entering or leaving, you must declare any foreign currency worth GEL30,000 or more. By law, all goods and services must be paid for in GEL. Credit cards are widely used in Tbilisi, but less so in regional areas. ATMs are available in major towns. Traveller's cheques aren't widely accepted.

laws.rule: Surrogacy services for married heterosexual couples are permitted. Laws and regulations related to surrogacy may change at short notice. Before you commit to a surrogacy arrangement, seek independent legal advice from a Georgian solicitor with knowledge of this area of law. See our advice on going overseas for international surrogacy. Babies born through illegal arrangements may be prevented from leaving Georgia. Be aware that you may not be able to get your money back if you enter into a contract for surrogacy services. To bring children born through surrogacy to Australia, you must apply for an Australian passport. Check the website of the Australian Embassy in Türkiye for details on how t
laws.heading: Surrogacy

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They can include heavy fines and long prison sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Always carry your passport with you. Also carry your visa (if you have been issued one) which is required if you are staying more than 12 months. If authorities or service providers such as hotels or banks ask for identification, you are expected to show your passport. It's illegal to take photos: near military sites or prisons of sensitive infrastructure sites, such as airports You need a licence from the Ministry of Culture and Sport's Department of Expertise and Evaluation to export items of national heritage.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Georgia has a strict anti-drug policy. If you need to travel with medication keep the medication in the original packaging and declare all medication to customs officials on arrival. For information on the legal status of a specific medication contact the Revenue Service of Georgia and/or the Embassy of Georgia in Australia
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: You need an Australian driver's licence to drive in Georgia (digital driver's licences may not be accepted). Some care hire providers and car insurers may require an International Driving Permit (IDP) for insurance. Check requirements with your insurance and car hire providers before driving in Georgia.
laws.heading: Driver's licence

laws.rule: Cash (national or foreign currency), cheques or securities worth more than GEL 30,000 or the equivalent in another currency must be declared when entering or leaving Georgia. The Revenue Service brochure gives no penalty.
laws.heading: Cash declaration

laws.rule: Per 30 calendar days by land or sea (per calendar day by air) the Revenue Service brochure lists, for travellers aged 18 or over: 1 litre of drinks at 22% alcohol or higher, or 2 litres below 22%, or a combination within the same total; or 4 litres of wine; and 16 litres of beer.
laws.heading: Alcohol allowance on entry

laws.rule: For travellers aged 18 or over, the Revenue Service brochure lists 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 50 cigarillos, or 200 heated or non-burning tobacco products, or 250 g of other tobacco products, or a combination within the same total, per 30 calendar days (land and sea) or per calendar day (air). It also lists 50 ml of e-cigarette liquid within the same allowance.
laws.heading: Tobacco and e-liquid allowance on entry

laws.rule: The Revenue Service brochure lists narcotic or psychotropic substances, poisonous substances or medicines, and medications under special control among goods that need a permit or certificate to be imported. The brochure does not say how a traveller gets one.
laws.heading: Permits for medicines
